name: Lixisenatide
route: Once-daily injection under the skin within an hour before the first meal
status: FDA-approved 2016; standalone Adlyxin discontinued in 2023, still sold combined with insulin glargine as Soliqua 100/33
mechanism: Short-acting exendin-4-based GLP-1 agonist that mainly blunts the blood sugar rise after meals by slowing stomach emptying and boosting insulin
uses: Type 2 diabetes (with insulin glargine in Soliqua)

article.summary: Lixisenatide is a short-acting, once-daily GLP-1 drug for type 2 diabetes. Sold alone as Adlyxin until 2023, it is now available in the US only in Soliqua 100/33.
article.takeaway: Lixisenatide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist modeled on exendin-4, the Gila monster peptide behind exenatide. Unlike weekly GLP-1 drugs, it acts for only part of the day, so its main effect is taming the **blood sugar spike after a meal** by slowing the stomach.[^1] Its heart outcomes trial showed it was safe after a recent heart attack but gave no cardiovascular benefit.[^2] Sanofi stopped selling standalone Adlyxin in the US in 2023; lixisenatide lives on in Soliqua 100/33, a once-daily pen that pairs it with long-acting insulin glargine.[^3]
glance: Approved 2016 (Adlyxin and Soliqua 100/33); Adlyxin discontinued in the US in 2023
Type 2 diabetes, now as part of the insulin glargine combination Soliqua 100/33
Once a day under the skin, within the hour before the first meal
GetGoal and LixiLan programs, the 6,068-person ELIXA trial, and a Parkinson's disease trial

blocks.text: GLP-1 is a gut hormone that boosts insulin when glucose is high, curbs glucagon and slows digestion. Lixisenatide is a 44-amino-acid peptide based on exendin-4, with a short tail of lysines added to its end, which makes it resistant to the enzyme that breaks down natural GLP-1.

GLP-1 drugs fall into two groups. Long-acting ones such as dulaglutide keep the receptor switched on around the clock and mostly lower fasting glucose. Short-acting ones such as lixisenatide and twice-daily exenatide work in bursts and mainly lower post-meal glucose by holding food in the stomach longer.[^1] That makes lixisenatide a natural partner for basal insulin, which handles fasting glucose but not meals.

In the US, lixisenatide is now available only in Soliqua 100/33, approved with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. Soliqua is not meant for type 1 diabetes or ketoacidosis, and it should not be combined with mealtime insulin or another GLP-1 drug.[^3]

rows: 6,068 adults with type 2 diabetes and a recent heart attack or unstable angina
Major cardiovascular events in 13.4% vs 13.2% on placebo over about 2 years: safe, no benefit[^2]
Motor scores held steady (change -0.04) vs worsening of 3.04 points on placebo at 12 months[^4]

blocks.text: ELIXA's neutral result contrasts with the heart benefits later shown for several long-acting GLP-1 drugs. The Parkinson's trial was a small phase 2 study with frequent nausea, and its authors called for longer, larger trials before drawing conclusions.[^4]

Soliqua 100/33 pens hold insulin glargine and lixisenatide in a fixed ratio, so every dial setting delivers both. It is injected once a day within an hour before the first meal. Depending on prior insulin use, people start at 15 or 30 units and adjust by 2-4 units a week based on fasting glucose, up to 60 units (which carries 20 mcg of lixisenatide). Any previous basal insulin or GLP-1 drug is stopped first.[^3]

items: **Common:** low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhea, colds and headache
**Serious but uncommon:** pancreatitis, severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, gallbladder disease and kidney injury from dehydration
**Insulin-related risks:** hypoglycemia, low potassium, and dosing errors if pens are confused
**Not recommended** with severe gastroparesis or end-stage kidney disease; tell anesthesia teams because of slowed stomach emptying[^3]

blocks.text: In ELIXA, lixisenatide did not raise rates of severe hypoglycemia, pancreatitis, pancreatic tumors or allergic reactions compared with placebo.[^2]

evidence.label: Strong for glucose control; neutral heart outcomes
evidence.text: Lixisenatide's effects on blood sugar and its cardiovascular safety were established in randomized trials, including ELIXA.[^2] It has not shown heart protection, and its Parkinson's data come from one phase 2 trial.[^4]

faq.a: No. Sanofi discontinued standalone Adlyxin in the US at the start of 2023 for business reasons. Lixisenatide is still available inside Soliqua 100/33.
Basal insulin mainly controls fasting glucose, while a short-acting GLP-1 drug targets the rise after meals.[^1] Combining them in one pen means a single injection a day.

faq.q: Is lixisenatide used for Parkinson's disease?
faq.a: Not outside research. A 2024 phase 2 trial found less motor decline over 12 months, but nausea was common and a larger trial is needed.[^4]

faq.q: How is it different from semaglutide?
faq.a: Lixisenatide is short-acting and taken daily, mostly affects post-meal glucose and showed no heart benefit. [Semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide) is weekly, lowers glucose and weight more and has proven cardiovascular benefit.
